entry.title: Unauthenticated SQL Injection In Channel Software WebAlliance eCommerce
entry.content:
vulnerability · sqli · CVE-2026-108065

CVE-2026-108065 affects Channel Software WebAlliance eCommerce, an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the GetUser SOAP method's sUserID parameter that fails to properly escape user input. The vulnerability is critical (CVSS 9.8) and allows attackers to extract sensitive data including PII and passwords, or execute system commands if the database runs with admin privileges; exploitation via time-based SQL injection and MSSQL stacked queries is trivial and no evidence of wild exploitation is reported but the public PoC increases risk. Organizations running WebAlliance eCommerce should immediately block access to /preapproval.asmx endpoint as a temporary mitigation and contact Channel Software for a patched version, as the vendor has not released a fix as of October 2026.

entry.title: From One Account to Every Mailbox: Breaking Zimbra's Identity Boundaries (Part 1)
entry.content:
vulnerability · multi · CVE-2026-10631, CVE-2026-50055, CVE-2026-73571, CVE-2026-93635, CVE-2026-93637

Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) contains five account-related vulnerabilities affecting authentication, mailbox authorization, and mail filtering: CVE-2026-93637 (GraphQL authentication rate-limit bypass, CVSS 3.7), CVE-2026-93635 (LDAP filter injection, CVSS 5.3), CVE-2026-73571 (email impersonation via SaveDraftRequest, CVSS 8.3), CVE-2026-10631 (EWS cross-user mailbox access, CVSS 6.5), and CVE-2026-50055 (Sieve notify forwarding-restriction bypass, CVSS 6.5). CVE-2026-73571, CVE-2026-10631, and CVE-2026-50055 are confirmed fixed in ZCS 10.1.17–10.1.20; fixes for CVE-2026-93637 and CVE-2026-93635 were not publicly listed at publication. No evidence of active exploitation in the wild is mentioned, but the high-severity email impersonation flaw and the cross-user mailbox access vulnerability allow full account compromise chains when chained with subsequent findings. Affected organizations must immediately upgrade to ZCS 10.1.20 or later, inspect existing Sieve rules for illicit notify actions, and review EWS access logs for suspicious cross-account operations.

entry.title: CVE-2026-97229: Critical Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in GitLab
entry.content:
vulnerability · integer-overflow-rce · CVE-2026-97229

GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions (CE/EE) versions 19.2 through 19.4.1 contain a critical integer overflow (CWE-190) in the CI/CD regular expression compiler that enables unauthenticated remote code execution with a CVSS score of 10.0. An attacker must commit a malicious .gitlab-ci.yml to a repository with UTF-8 characters; when evaluated, an encoding recompilation triggers integer overflow in Onigmo regex engine, allowing arbitrary code execution as the GitLab git user. While no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation exists, Rapid7 has independently reproduced code execution on unpatched instances. Organizations must immediately upgrade affected self-managed instances to versions 19.2.8, 19.3.5, or 19.4.2 outside normal patch cycles; GitLab.com and Dedicated are unaffected. Interim mitigation includes restricting anonymous access and preventing untrusted users from creating public projects, though these do not remediate the underlying vulnerability.

entry.title: SMTP is the key: BPFDoor and AVERAT hitting the network edge
entry.content:
red-team · c2, persistence, evasion

BPFDoor and AVERAT Linux implants target telecom and network-edge appliances including mail-security gateways, DVRs, and NAS devices in South Korea and Taiwan. BPFDoor is a passive Berkeley Packet Filter-based backdoor that uses kernel-level packet interception with magic-byte triggers (evolved to hide in HTTPS POST requests to evade detection), while AVERAT is a modular implant beaconing via SMTP to blend with legitimate mail traffic and supporting ten concurrent shell sessions, file operations, and dynamic C2 reconfiguration. Both families are actively exploited in the wild; BPFDoor variants use regional process spoofing (SpamSniper in Korea, Oracle/Sniper daemons in telecom infrastructure) and AVERAT infrastructure comprises compromised consumer/SMB appliances in Taiwan acting as operational relays consistent with China-nexus ORB networks. Organizations should hunt for processes with deleted executables (/proc/pid/exe pointing to deleted), monitor outbound SMTP from non-mail services to consumer-grade hosts, detect raw packet sockets and BPF filters on non-packet-capture systems, and restrict management access to edge appliances while preserving process forensics and DNS records; patch end-of-life appliances where possible and segment network-edge devices.

entry.title: WordPress Backdoor Rebuilds Itself After Cleanup Using Files, Database, and Shared Memory
entry.content:
red-team · persistence

WordPress sites are targeted by the SC backdoor, which employs multiple persistence mechanisms including file-based, database, and shared memory storage to rebuild itself after cleanup attempts. The malware uses "SC_" markers and operates as a self-healing mesh architecture, making traditional removal difficult even after initial infection mitigation. This represents a high-severity threat as it enables attackers to maintain long-term access despite remediation efforts. Recommended actions include comprehensive malware scanning with updated signatures, complete database audits to remove injected entries, shared memory inspection, file integrity monitoring post-cleanup, and immediate patching of WordPress core, plugins, and themes to eliminate initial compromise vectors.

entry.title: PyJWT: Asymmetric-PEM detection bypass: whitespace/line-ending-mutated public keys skip the HS/asymmetric confusion guard (CVE-2026-102268)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-102268, CVE-2026-107722

PyJWT versions prior to patching are vulnerable to asymmetric-HMAC confusion attacks when decoding JWT tokens if the allow-list contains both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms (CVE-2026-102268, critical severity). The vulnerability exploits a bypass in PyJWT's PEM format detection where whitespace or line-ending mutations in public keys cause the `is_pem_format` regex to fail, allowing an attacker with a valid HMAC secret to forge tokens that pass asymmetric signature verification. This impacts deployments mixing algorithm types in the decode allow-list and passing PEM keys as raw bytes/text. Immediately update PyJWT to the patched version and audit configurations to follow RFC 8725 best practices by using single asymmetric algorithms in decode allow-lists rather than mixing HS/asymmetric options.

This is rated critical severity and appears to have active exploitation potential given its nature as a supply-chain attack vector on archive handling. Users should immediately update to a patched version and consider validating archive contents before extraction in production environments.

entry.title: New Spectre-v2 BTR Attack Leaks Linux Memory Despite Existing Defenses
entry.content:
vulnerability · speculative-execution

A new Spectre-v2 variant called Branch Target Reuse (BTR) affects JIT engines in web browsers, language runtimes, and OS kernels across multiple CPU vendors by exploiting branch predictor reuse to leak sensitive memory despite existing mitigations. The vulnerability bypasses current Spectre-v2 defenses by leveraging indirect branch target predictions, enabling attackers to extract kernel and application memory from JavaScript or native code. Severity appears high given the broad affected scope and kernel-level access potential, though no widespread in-the-wild exploitation has been reported yet. Mitigation requires microcode updates and software-level defenses targeting branch prediction isolation; vendors should prioritize patching JIT implementations and evaluating additional branch target buffer protections.
